summary: Year 6 pupils learn to translate shapes on a four-quadrant coordinate grid (adding/subtracting signed amounts to matching coordinates) and to reflect shapes in the x- or y-axis by negating exactly one coordinate. The goal is to DERIVE the sign rules from geometry — points move perpendicular to the mirror axis, so the coordinate measuring distance from that axis flips sign while the other stays — rather than memorise a swap. Core errors: changing the wrong coordinate (reflecting in the wrong axis), sliding instead of reflecting (no reversal), wrong translation signs for left/down moves, and reversing the ordered pair.
misconceptions: Reflecting in the x-axis but changing the sign of the WRONG coordinate (negating x instead of y), effectively reflecting in the other axis.
Reflecting by sliding/translating the shape rather than reflecting it, so the image is not reversed.
Getting the translation sign wrong — adding when the move is left or down instead of subtracting.
Reversing the coordinate pair (writing the y-value before the x-value) when stating image vertices.

activities.title: Predict, then reflect: watch the single coordinate flip
steps: On a four-quadrant grid, start with a triangle plotted in the second quadrant and its vertices labelled with coordinates.
Before anything moves, choose 'reflect in the x-axis' and write down what you predict each vertex will become.
Run the reflection: watch each vertex move perpendicular to the x-axis (vertically, to the opposite side) while, in a coordinate table, only the y-value changes sign and x stays the same.
If a real mirror or Mira is available, stand it on the x-axis to check the image faces the opposite way and sits the same distance from the axis.
Now, starting from the SAME triangle, reflect in the y-axis instead and predict again: this time the shape flips sideways (perpendicular to the y-axis) and only x changes sign.
Compare the two results on the same vertex, e.g. (−4, 1) → (−4, −1) in the x-axis but (−4, 1) → (4, 1) in the y-axis.
activities.insight: Reflecting in the x-axis flips the shape vertically, so the y-coordinate (vertical distance from the x-axis) negates and x is unchanged; reflecting in the y-axis flips it horizontally, so x negates and y is unchanged. The axis you reflect IN is the mirror and points move perpendicular to it.

activities.title: Translate by signed changes — predict before plotting
steps: Take a triangle on the grid and a translation instruction such as '3 squares right and 2 squares down'.
Treat each direction as a signed change to the matching coordinate: right adds to x, left subtracts from x, up adds to y, down subtracts from y. So '3 right, 2 down' gives (x, y) → (x+3, y−2).
Predict the new coordinates of every vertex BEFORE plotting, then plot and check against the grid.
Say back how the whole shape kept its orientation (a slide does not reverse the shape).
activities.insight: Translation adds or subtracts a signed amount to the matching coordinate and preserves orientation; left and down are negative changes, not additions.

activities.title: Contrast slide versus reflect, and keep the pair in order
steps: Reflect a triangle in the x-axis and separately translate the same triangle 'down' by a fixed amount; place the two results side by side.
Describe how they differ: the reflected image is reversed and equidistant on the opposite side of the axis; the translated image faces the same way and simply slid.
Find a vertex that sits ON the mirror axis, e.g. (0, 4) on the y-axis, and reflect in that axis: note it stays fixed.
When listing every image vertex, write x before y ('along then up/down') and check one plotted point matches the pair you wrote.
activities.insight: Reflection reverses sense and is equidistant across the mirror; translation preserves sense. Points on the mirror axis map to themselves. Ordered pairs are always (x, y).

activities.title: Diagnose with paired axis items (assessment)
steps: Answer items such as '(−4, 1) reflected in the x-axis = ?' where the correct answer is (−4, −1), the wrong-coordinate answer (4, 1) and the reversed-pair answer (−1, −4) are offered as options.
Complete fill-in-the-blank image coordinates after a stated translation.
Plot a reflection by drawing the image, then list its vertices.
Explain in words why only one coordinate changed for each reflection.
activities.insight: Picking the correct image while rejecting wrong-axis and reversed-pair distractors, plotting the image correctly, and explaining why only one coordinate changes together show the rule is reasoned rather than guessed.

checkQuestion: Give a four-quadrant grid with a small triangle plotted in the second quadrant (vertices labelled with their coordinates). Say: 'First, translate this triangle 3 squares right and 2 squares down, and write the new coordinates of each vertex. Then, starting from the original, reflect it in the x-axis and list the reflected vertices. Finally, tell me how the coordinates changed in each case, and why.' Set the task and WATCH which coordinate the child changes and whether the reflected image is reversed — do not state the rules.
checkAnswer: For the translation, each vertex gains 3 on x and loses 2 on y (right +x, down −y). For the reflection in the x-axis, each vertex keeps its x and negates its y — (x, y) → (x, −y) — so the image sits the same distance below the axis as the original is above, reversed in sense. The child explains that translating adds/subtracts to the coordinates while reflecting in the x-axis changes the sign of the y-coordinate only (and reflecting in the y-axis would change x only), because points move perpendicular to the mirror axis.
